subject: On-prem cluster: control plane placement, node affinity patterns, and storage slab proposal

Subject: Ironbridge preflight: control plane, node sizing, and 'storage slab' question

Neha/Marissa —

Thanks for the time on Friday. We're consolidating our requirements for the on-prem private cluster you folks will be standing up in our DC (Rack 12). Two quick asks as we lock the scope:

1) We want the control plane to survive a single rack failure without triggering a full cluster rebuild. Does Redwood recommend a two-rack control-plane quorum with etcd voting proxies or host all control-plane components on dedicated nodes?

2) We're trying a new pattern internally called a "storage slab" — logical grouping of PV classes by IO and retention (hot-slab, warm-slab, cold-archive). We'd like Redwood's opinion on persistent volume topology and eviction behavior if multiple tenants burst IO against the hot-slab.

Attached is our rack sketch and a spreadsheet of current expected IOPS per tenant. Can someone from your side propose a placement schematic + node affinity pattern we can review?

Cheers,

Kevin —

Thanks for the clear ask and the IOPS sheet. High level responses below; I'll attach a concise diagram (controlplane-placement-diagram.v1.png) and a short proposal (storage-slab-proposal.pdf) after we sync internally.

Control plane resilience
- Recommendation: run a 3-node control plane across two failure domains (two racks + one control-plane witness in a third fault domain if available). This gives quorum safety for single-rack loss while keeping etcd latency reasonable.
- Option B (if you cannot spare 3 physical hosts): 2 control-plane nodes + external etcd voting proxy — increases operational complexity and reduces robustness; we only take this route when hardware footprint is strict.

Node pools and affinity pattern
- Suggest 3 node-pools for workloads: gpu/accel (if any), general compute, IO-optimized (NVMe). Use topology-aware ephemeral affinity: prefer local zone/rack but allow cross-rack scheduling when local capacity is exhausted.
- For control-plane components, pin to dedicated control-plane nodes (taint: dedicated=control:NoSchedule) and set kubelet eviction thresholds at the node level to avoid disk pressure cascading into control-plane eviction.

Storage slab guidance (hot/warm/cold)
- Hot-slab: NVMe local PVs with hostPath/NVMe CSI, low-latency, striped LVM when multiple devices present. Use a quota controller (CSI + PVC admission webhook) to limit per-tenant IOPS share.
- Warm-slab: network-attached SSDs (iSCSI/roce), replication factor 2, set io_kill limits at cgroup level to protect noisy neighbors.
- Cold-archive: object-store-backed (on-prem S3 gateway) with lifecycle rules.

Next steps: we'll produce a placement diagram showing control-plane across Racks 12/13 with witness in Rack 9 and a node affinity matrix mapping tenant categories to slab classes. Can you confirm whether Rack 9 is available as a witness and the maximum number of dedicated control-plane servers you can allocate?

cc: Marissa (Customer Eng) and Jonas (Solutions) for operational runbook inputs.

Kevin — quick technical answers and attachments below. Attaching the control plane diagram and slab proposal to this thread (controlplane-placement-diagram.v1.png, storage-slab-proposal.pdf).

Witness design
- Witness: we recommend a lightweight VM running only the etcd arbiter (voting proxy) in Rack 9. It should have 2 vCPU / 8GB RAM and a small SSD for WAL shipping. It does not need to be a full k8s node.

BOM / NICs
- Control-plane host: 4 vCPU reserved (bare-metal equivalent 8-core), 32GB RAM, dual 25GbE NICs (one for cluster overlay + one for management/backup), 1 x 240GB NVMe for OS + etcd WAL.

Eviction policy recommendations
- Set kube-reserved and system-reserved values on nodes hosting control-plane and IO-optimized pools.
- For app nodes on hot-slab: eviction.signal thresholds should be disk pressure at 95% with eviction grace of 5m for critical PVCs and 30s for best-effort.
- Implement a two-stage eviction: soft eviction with QoS demotion (reduce throttles) followed by hard eviction only after sustained 10m pressure or >98% disk fill.

Testing plan (staging)
- We will provide a small test harness that simulates noisy-tenant IO (attached as a script in the Drive link). Run the harness against your staging hot-slab and evaluate 95th percentile latency. We'll iterate cgroup/io limits until noisy neighbors are within SLA.

Next steps: Neha/Marissa to produce finalized BOM and we will schedule a 45-minute walkthrough with your ops team tomorrow.
